decisions.commercialLayer: BUILD — user takes direct clients. Accepts overlap with scssconsulting.com.au.
decisions.commercialStrategy: Compete on solo-specialist long-tail only. Do not target 'healthcare software development company australia' — that SERP is agencies and listicles.
decisions.contentClearance: REQUIRED before writing. Every post carries a `clearanceNeeded` field; confirm all in one pass.

pillar.title: Building Healthcare Software for the Australian Market
pillar.rationale: The engineer's view of AU health compliance and integration. Every head-term SERP is held by agencies with 1000+ project counts and listicle farms; this pillar deliberately targets the implementation layer none of them write about.
pillar.clearanceNeeded: Which of the three layers you can speak to from the real build, and at what depth. The pillar summarises every spoke, so it inherits the union of their clearance requirements.

clusters.name: Compliance as engineering requirements
clusters.gap: Every result is either the regulator's own site (ahpra.gov.au, oaic.gov.au) or a generic privacy-SaaS blog. Zero developer-facing content. Google's own summary for the AHPRA query said results 'focus more on practitioner obligations rather than detailed software development specifications'.

posts.title: AHPRA's virtual care rules, translated into software requirements
posts.clearanceNeeded: Which AHPRA/virtual-care obligations actually shaped Cannabiz Elite's build — consent capture, practitioner identity display, record-keeping.

posts.title: The 13 Australian Privacy Principles as a build checklist for health apps
posts.clearanceNeeded: How consent, data minimisation and access/correction were implemented. Any privacy review or assessment output.

posts.title: What 'Privacy Act ready' actually means in your architecture
posts.clearanceNeeded: Hosting region, encryption approach, tenancy model, retention policy. Whether the architecture can be described at all.

clusters.name: National infrastructure integration
clusters.gap: Dominated by developer.digitalhealth.gov.au and implementer.digitalhealth.gov.au specs plus eRx's own vendor pages. Exactly one independent implementation write-up exists across both SERPs. Specs tell you the contract; nobody documents what it is like to actually ship against them.

posts.title: Integrating My Health Record via the FHIR Gateway: a real walkthrough
posts.keyword: my health record fhir gateway integration
posts.clearanceNeeded: Whether My Health Record integration was in scope; if so, the conformance steps, auth model and what failed first.

posts.title: eRx Script Exchange integration for telehealth prescribing
posts.clearanceNeeded: Whether eRx or another script exchange was integrated, and the token/dispense flow as built.

posts.title: The Healthcare Identifiers Service: the prerequisite nobody documents
posts.clearanceNeeded: Whether the HI Service was used, and what the onboarding actually required.

clusters.name: Clinic systems and clinical workflow
clusters.gap: Vendor docs and directory listings only. The modelling question — how you represent a prescription, a consult or a script in a commerce/order system — is not addressed anywhere, and is the single most defensible thing Cannabiz Elite can speak to.

posts.title: Modelling prescriptions as orders: Medusa v2 workflows for a telehealth clinic
posts.clearanceNeeded: The prescription/consult data model in Medusa v2 — the single most valuable and most likely sensitive detail.

posts.title: Integrating with Best Practice, Cliniko and Halaxy: what each one expects
posts.keyword: cliniko halaxy best practice api integration
posts.clearanceNeeded: Which clinic systems were integrated and what each demanded in practice.

posts.title: Telehealth MBS item numbers and the billing logic they imply
posts.clearanceNeeded: Whether MBS billing logic was implemented and how item numbers were handled.

clusters.name: Commercial conversion layer
clusters.gap: Head terms are held by agencies with 1,000+ delivered projects and by scssconsulting.com.au. The service page therefore targets solo-specialist long-tail — 'developer' not 'company', and named integrations rather than generic 'healthcare software' — where a named engineer with a shipped Australian telehealth build outranks a generic agency page.

posts.title: Australian healthcare software development
posts.clearanceNeeded: Which capabilities you can claim publicly and in your own name rather than the agency's.

posts.title: Cannabiz Elite — Australian telehealth clinic management
posts.keyword: telehealth clinic management system case study
posts.clearanceNeeded: Client naming permission, plus any publishable metric — launch timeline, clinic count, transaction volume.

excluded.keyword: hire developer medical practice management software australia
excluded.reason: SERP returns software directories (Capterra, SourceForge, SoftwareSuggest) and vendors (Shexie, MediRecords), not development services. Google reads the intent as 'find practice management software to buy', not 'hire someone to build it'. Zero URL overlap with any development-services SERP. Targeting it would rank a service page against a buyer looking for an off-the-shelf product.

Held by agencies with 1000+ delivered projects (Appinventiv, DesignPluz, Vrinsoft) and listicle farms (vocal.media, techwize). A one-person site does not enter this auction, and it is the same SERP the employer already competes in.
